transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. I am sorry to hear that happened. Running a microwave completely empty for 10 minutes is very hard on the components, as there is nothing inside to absorb the energy. To answer your question: it may or may not be broken, but you must stop using it immediately. Because there is an active burning hazard and potential internal damage from overheating, this appliance needs to be checked by a qualified engineer before it is used again. Do not try to run it to "test" if it works. If you are comfortable doing so safely (with the unit unplugged), you can check the interior for any obvious melted plastic or burnt marks on that side panel, but please do not attempt to open the casing yourself.

Thanks. It's only turned off at the switch, so it's still plugged in. There was some smoke coming out of the side vents when we stopped it, and I can see a brownish mark on the side wall panel inside. The burnt electrical smell is fading but still there. Should I just bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If there are flames or smoke is still coming from it, keep away, don't open the door of an oven, microwave or dryer that is on fire, switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.

claimsRejected.claim: The "horrible smell" suggests something has burnt inside—this could be food residue, a plastic component, or the waveguide cover (the small flat panel on the side wall).

candidates: Burnt plastic or food residue inside the cavity (high)
Damage to the waveguide cover (mica sheet) (medium)

reading.symptom: horrible smell after running empty for 10 minutes

plan: They asked: "Is it broken?" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "horrible smell after running empty for 10 minutes". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

hazards.clause: there was some smoke coming out of the side vents when we stopped it
